toolCallDetails.arguments: {"path":"snake_openai-gpt-6.1-sol_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete standalone HTML file with inline CSS and JavaScript, no external dependencies: polished classic two-player Snake game on exactly 30x30 grid. Dark navy arcade aesthetic, mint and amber snakes, visible grid, responsive square canvas, attractive header, score cards for both players, start menu overlay with selectable Human vs Human, CPU vs Human, CPU vs CPU modes and start button, game over overlay with winner/draw, reason, final scores and restart/menu buttons. Instructions visible: P1 WASD, P2 arrows; in CPU vs Human P1 is CPU and P2 human. R restarts current mode, Enter starts/restarts, Escape returns to menu, Space pauses/resumes with pause overlay. Prevent default browser scrolling for gameplay keys. Human direction changes must disallow reverse and allow only one accepted change per simulation tick. Continuous fixed step movement ~120ms using requestAnimationFrame timestamp accumulator (reset timing on pause/window blur; auto pause blur). Two snakes start safely separated at x=7,y=10 facing right and x=22,y=19 facing left, length four. Food randomly on unoccupied cells, eating increments score and grows by one; one shared food. Simultaneous move resolution: walls, own and opponent body (tails vacate only if not eating), same target head collision and head swaps; any death ends match, survivor wins or simultaneous deaths draw. No wrapping. Handle board-full finish without infinite food placement. Render clean colored rounded segments and distinguish heads with eyes, glowing food and subtle grid. CPU must genuinely search routes to food using BFS on occupied-grid (allow its vacating tail when appropriate), not simply random steering; filter reversal/unsafe next cells, avoid opponent likely head targets where feasible, use flood-fill reachable space as survival fallback if food unreachable; no infinite loops. Ensure AI operates on pre-tick shared state and direction choices don't mutate movement while planning. Provide responsive controls and optional on-screen arrow buttons targeting human player (P2 for cpu vs human, choose P1/P2 in human vs human). All screens/buttons functional, aria labels and keyboard focus styling, explanatory labels for modes and CPU tags in score cards. Keep code readable in English. Initialize draw/menu immediately, only start loop once, state-driven screens and no duplicated listeners. Write the full finished file."}
